_comment: The repair loop's hands, and only these. The loop works in a scratch copy under $HOME/Documents/agent-tornado/work and cannot write anywhere else: write-file's root is that folder, and loop.js refuses any write that does not land inside the run's own copy. Nothing here can reach the repo it copied from -- copy-repo is the only hand that names it, and it only reads.

tools.name: Make the work folder
tools.description: Create the scratch folder for a run. Plumbing for the repair loop; it takes no clause binding.

path.description: Absolute folder to create. Parents are created too.

tools.name: Copy a repo into the scratch folder
tools.description: Copy a repository into the run's scratch folder so the loop can edit a copy and never the original. The bridge resolves and echoes both paths back in the call's plan, which is how the loop learns where the copy actually landed.

src.description: Absolute path to the repository to copy. Read only.

dst.description: Absolute path of the scratch copy. Must not already exist.

tools.name: Write a file in the scratch copy
tools.description: Replace one file inside the run's scratch copy. Always asks first, and the root is the scratch folder -- the repo the copy came from is not writable by this hand even if something asked.

path.description: Absolute path inside the scratch folder.

content.description: The whole file, as UTF-8. Capped at 64 KB.

tools.name: Run a node test suite
tools.description: Run `node --test` with the given folder as its working directory, so every test file under it runs. This is the loop's verdict: exit 0 means green.

repo.description: Absolute folder to run the suite in -- the scratch copy, not your repo.

tools.name: Run a Python test suite
tools.description: Run `python3 -m unittest` with the given folder as its working directory. The same verdict as run-suite, for a Python repo.

repo.description: Absolute folder to run the suite in -- the scratch copy, not your repo.

tools.name: Summarise the difference
tools.description: `git diff --no-index --stat` between your repo and the scratch copy, so you can see which files the loop touched without reading a whole patch. Exit 1 means the two differ, which is the expected answer once anything changed.

b.description: Absolute path to the scratch copy.

tools.name: Read the difference in full
tools.description: The whole `git diff --no-index` patch between your repo and the scratch copy, clipped at 64 KB. This is what you read before copying anything back.

b.description: Absolute path to the scratch copy.
